physical: Joule heating: A current through a resistance dissipates power as heat in proportion to the resistance and the square of the current. P = I² × R
reflected_formula: [no partner: power P] = [no partner: current I]² × [electrical resistance R → the gap]
reflected_sentence: The relationship turns around: the loss that grew with the gap shrinks as receptivity grows; the rate of loss and the flow that carries it have no partners, so only the direction crosses.
rule_reason: One cost (carrying the current without loss) rises with electrical resistance, which the fixed table says carries resistance. One resistance-cost is an odd number, so the reading turns: what is lost under more resistance is kept under more receptivity.
unmapped_terms: current (electric) (the bare word 'electric' has the partner Idle, but the quantity current has no row and I did not compose one)
electrical resistance (no table row; only the flipped condition 'receptivity' and 'the gap' are legal for it)
interpretation: Where the gap is wide, more is lost; where receptivity is full, less is. The flow that carries it, and the loss itself, have no partners.
closing: The rule decided on its own: electrical resistance is fixed as carrying resistance, the one cost rises with it, the row turns. The ambiguity is in the vocabulary: 'electric' maps to Idle as a co-creating partner, but electric current is a flow with no row, and electrical resistance has no row beyond the rule's own flip to receptivity and 'the gap'. I used only those legal words. The square of the current has no frozen image, so the monotone claim could not be written in frozen words.
